user.title: Connect to INIM Prime
user.description: Enter the address and LAN password of your INIM PrimeX panel.

data_description.name: Friendly name for this panel — used for the device and entity names (e.g. "Allarme").
data_description.local_6004_password: The panel's LAN/programming password (default 'pass'). Home Assistant talks to the panel only over its local protocol (TCP 6004); PrimeX/Prime firmware 4.x and 5.00 are supported.

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate INIM Prime
reauth_confirm.description: The panel at {host} could not be read with the stored LAN password. Enter the panel's LAN password to continue.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure INIM Prime
reconfigure.description: Update the name, address or LAN password of your INIM PrimeX panel without removing the integration.

data_description.name: Friendly name for this panel — used for the device and entity names (e.g. "Allarme").
data_description.local_6004_password: The panel's LAN/programming password (default 'pass'). Home Assistant talks to the panel only over its local protocol (TCP 6004); PrimeX/Prime firmware 4.x and 5.00 are supported.

error.cannot_connect: Could not read the panel over its local protocol (TCP 6004). Check the address, the LAN password and that the panel is reachable.
error.unsupported_firmware: This panel firmware is not supported: its memory map is not known. PrimeX/Prime firmware 4.x and 5.00 are supported.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Choose the areas to show, how zones are labelled and grouped, enable push mode, and whether a user code is required.

data.require_code: Require a user code to arm or disarm

data_description.areas: Panel areas that get entities in Home Assistant (alarm panel, alarm memory, clear button). The choice is kept by area number, so renaming an area on the panel keeps it. Unselected areas get no entities (existing ones are removed) but still work in scenarios and commands. Areas added on the panel later stay hidden until you select them here.
data_description.label_language: Language used to guess each zone's device class (icon) from its name. Auto follows Home Assistant's language.
data_description.group_by_room: Place each zone (and its bypass switch) under a per-room device, guessed from the zone name. You then assign each room device to a Home Assistant area.
data_description.require_code: When on, Home Assistant asks for an INIM user code and the panel validates it before each arm or disarm. The code is never stored. By default the panel accepts any command over the LAN once the protocol password is known, so this adds a per-user check on Home Assistant's side. The one-tap scenario buttons are disabled while this is on, because a button cannot prompt for a code — use the area alarm panels, which show a keypad.

panels.title: Alarm panels
panels.description: Panels are extra alarm controls that arm or disarm several areas at once. Choose how to create one.

menu_options.panel_add_inverse: Create from a detected scenario pair
menu_options.panel_add_areas: Create from a set of areas

panel_add_areas.title: Panel from areas
panel_add_areas.description: The panel arms or disarms these areas together, offering away, home and night.

panel_add_scenarios.title: Panel from two scenarios
panel_add_scenarios.description: Arming applies the arm scenario; disarming applies the disarm scenario.

panel_add_inverse.title: Panels from detected pairs
panel_add_inverse.description: These scenario pairs arm and disarm exactly the same areas. Pick the ones to turn into panels; each takes the name of its arm scenario and can be renamed or removed later.

panel_edit.title: Edit a panel
panel_edit.description: Pick the panel to edit; its name and areas or scenarios follow.

panel_edit_form.title: Edit panel
panel_edit_form.description: Change the name and the areas or scenarios. The panel keeps its identity.

abort.no_areas: No areas are available on this panel yet.

zones_not_ready.message: The command was rejected because one or more zones are not ready (open or in fault).

code_required.message: A user code is required to arm or disarm this area.

invalid_code.message: The panel rejected that code. Check the INIM user code and that it is allowed on this area.

code_check_failed.message: Could not verify the code with the panel, so nothing was armed or disarmed: {error}

forced_arm_bad_target.message: Entity {entity_id} is not an INIM Prime entity.

forced_arm_single_target.message: Forced arm accepts exactly one target entity.

forced_arm_mode_with_scenario.message: Provide either a scenario or an arm mode, not both.

forced_arm_area_or_scenario.message: Target an area (with a mode), or provide a scenario name.

forced_arm_unbypassable_zones.message: Cannot force-arm: these zones can't be bypassed and are still open: {zones}.

event_log_bad_target.message: Entity {entity_id} is not an INIM Prime entity.

event_log_single_target.message: Get event log accepts exactly one target entity.

native_command_uncertain.message: The native command may have reached the panel, but its outcome is unknown ({error}). It was not retried; check the panel state before trying again.

bypass_not_applied.message: The panel did not apply the bypass change for zone {zone}.

scenario_not_supported.message: This scenario cannot be applied: it has no single target mode per area, or the panel has areas beyond the ones a scenario definition covers.

panel_not_supported.message: This panel cannot run that command right now (a referenced scenario is gone, or it has no areas): {panel}.

get_event_log.name: Get event log
get_event_log.description: Read the panel's stored event log over the local protocol (read-only) and return it.

entity_id.name: Target
entity_id.description: Any INIM Prime entity — identifies the panel to read.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: Return only the most recent N events (0 = all).

arm_forced.name: Arm (forced)
arm_forced.description: Arm an area or apply a scenario even when zones are open, by bypassing the open zones first.

entity_id.name: Target
entity_id.description: An INIM Prime area (alarm control panel) — identifies the panel.

scenario.name: Scenario
scenario.description: Scenario to apply, by name (e.g. Ins.Notte). Use instead of a mode.

mode.name: Arm mode
mode.description: Arm mode when the target is an area (ignored for a scenario).

allow_partial.name: Allow partial arm
allow_partial.description: Arm even if some open zones cannot be bypassed (reports which stayed open). Off = refuse if any cannot be bypassed.
